analysis.session_summary: Japan dominated the tape: the 15:15 'yentervention' headline sent USD/JPY -131.8 pips to 158.846 and CHF/JPY -181.3 pips, leaving JPY as the strongest major at +0.88%. NZD was the weakest major at -0.966% despite an inline RBNZ hike, with NZD/USD down -46.3 pips and AUD/NZD up +127.1 pips. The BoC hold at 2.25% strengthened CAD, driving USD/CAD -58.7 pips. Risk assets leaned positive with SPX +0.343%, VIX -1.54%, and Brent +1.731%.

themes.evidence: 15:15 'We've got ourselves another yentervention'; USD/JPY -131.8 pips, CHF/JPY -181.3 pips, JPY mean +0.88%.
OCR printed in line at 2.75% but NZD still weakened -0.585%; NZD/USD -46.3 pips, AUD/NZD +127.1 pips, NZD mean -0.966%.
Overnight Rate held at 2.25% inline; CAD strengthened 0.164%; USD/CAD -58.7 pips with close in 0.08 of range.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped in a 41.9-pip range, with the largest up-leg +36.3 pips partly yentervention-driven, leaving close at 1.15874 and only +1.8 pips on the day.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD faded early weakness with a sharp 37.9-pip yentervention bounce, then gave back gains to close -20.3 pips at 1.34942.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD initially fell with RBNZ spillover before recovering +45.3 pips on yen intervention flows, closing +18.0 pips at 0.7168.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD collapsed -88.0 pips on RBNZ OCR/Monetary Policy Statement, bounced +40.2 pips, but still closed -46.3 pips at 0.58456.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY bled lower in a 215.7-pip range, with the dominant -152.3-pip down-leg linked to the yentervention headline, closing -131.8 pips at 158.846.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF saw a 41.8-pip up-leg on GDP spillover and a -36.7-pip yentervention down-leg, closing +7.9 pips at 0.81312.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD spiked +34.6 pips before the BoC hold and presser drove -92.4 pips lower, closing -58.7 pips at 1.38461 near the bottom of its range.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF chopped within 33.6 pips, with a 29.1-pip up-leg mid-session that faded into BoC-driven EUR weakness, closing +10.8 pips at 0.94219.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY was the biggest yen cross decliner with a -211.4-pip down-leg after yentervention, closing -181.3 pips at 195.343.
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD ripped +144.8 pips in one leg as RBNZ details hit NZD, closing +127.1 pips at 1.22615.
leg_notes.EUR/GBP: EUR/GBP chopped within a narrow 25.9-pip range, with the largest up-leg +23.1 pips and close +14.2 pips at 0.85866.
leg_notes.AUD/CHF: AUD/CHF recovered from an early -11.7-pip down-leg to close +20.1 pips at 0.58282, aided by a +24.7-pip late leg.
leg_notes.NZD/CHF: NZD/CHF dropped -54.5 pips on RBNZ news before bouncing +21.6 pips, still closing -33.1 pips at 0.47529.
leg_notes.USD/SEK: USD/SEK whipsawed in a wide 668.2-pip range with multiple risk/yentervention legs, closing +93.6 pips at 9.6243.
leg_notes.USD/NOK: USD/NOK faded after an early +91.6-pip leg and closed -109.2 pips at 9.31302, with a medium-confidence yentervention down-leg of -279.1 pips.
leg_notes.USD/ZAR: USD/ZAR initially jumped +406.3 pips then fell -1307.0 pips as risk rally/yentervention hit, closing -922.3 pips at 16.0561.
leg_notes.USD/MXN: USD/MXN whipsawed through 612 pips with conflict headlines and yentervention, closing +55.1 pips at 16.98732.
leg_notes.Brent/USD: Brent/USD rallied +269.6 pips initially, sold off -306.0 pips, then bounced +200.1 pips into the close, finishing +166.7 pips at 97.958.

polarity_reads.read: In-line 2.75% hike still saw NZD weaken -0.585%, implying a hawkish surprise was already priced and positioning used the as-expected outcome to sell.
Unscored, but follow-on NZD weakness of -0.193% confirms the negative NZD reaction had persistence beyond the initial print.
In-line 2.25% hold but CAD strengthened 0.164%, suggesting short-CAD positioning was caught or the statement lacked dovish follow-through.
Unscored, but another 0.114% CAD gain shows the CAD bid persisted as Macklem reiterated inflation is too high.
Beat of 0.4% vs 0.3% produced normal AUD strength of 0.084%, but too small to offset the RBNZ/yen spillover.
Miss of 38K vs 47K was ignored with the basket at -0.018%, inside the noise floor, so weak US labor data is not yet a USD driver.

scenarios.name: Yen intervention follow-through
scenarios.thesis: The market treats the 15:15 yentervention as a live policy shock; JPY strength extends and high-beta/carry FX stays pressured.
triggers: USD/JPY fails to reclaim the 159.71 headline print
RBNZ Gov Breman Speaks at 22:10 adds to NZD downside
scenarios.invalidation: USD/JPY closes back above the 215.7-pip day range high or risk FX rallies decisively.

pair_paths.rationale: Already -131.8 pips on the day with close at 0.28 of the 215.7-pip range, leaving room to extend lower.
CHF/JPY fell -181.3 pips and closed at 0.18 of its 258.3-pip range, so follow-through risk remains.
NZD is the weakest major at -0.966%; the 94.3-pip day range low is the extension target.
RBNZ-driven AUD/NZD strength of +127.1 pips can extend toward the 172.6-pip day range high.

scenarios.name: Central-bank repricing stabilizes
scenarios.thesis: BoC hold and RBNZ moves are absorbed; CAD and AUD outperform, USD stays mixed, and upcoming US data encourages risk recovery.
triggers: US Unemployment Claims prints in line or below 205K
scenarios.invalidation: A fresh yentervention headline or a sharp VIX reversal higher reopens the risk-off leg.

pair_paths.rationale: BoC hold with CAD strength and a close at 0.08 of the 101.9-pip range supports continuation lower.
After -0.966% NZD underperformance, a short squeeze can retrace the 94.3-pip day range.
AUD strength of +0.22% and the GDP beat support recovery through the 54.0-pip range.
No clear catalyst for EUR/USD; the 41.9-pip range remains intact around the 1.15874 close.

scenarios.name: US data floor for USD
scenarios.thesis: Strong Unemployment Claims and ISM Services data arrest the USD slide, forcing a consolidation of the yen and commodity moves.
triggers: US Unemployment Claims comes in below 205K
DXY/USD reclaims the 44.7-point day range upper half
scenarios.invalidation: A soft ISM below 54.1 or another yentervention headline sends USD lower again.

pair_paths.rationale: Strong US data would push EUR/USD toward the bottom of the 41.9-pip day range.
CHF CPI at 08:30 and a firmer USD can drive USD/CHF through its 45.4-pip range high.
Cable's -20.3-pip day and 46.3-pip range leave room for USD recovery to test the range low.

risks.why_it_matters: The tape had 42 headlines with multiple US-Iran strike items; a flare-up can reverse the risk-on backdrop and lift oil/havens.
JPY closed as the strongest major at +0.88%; further intervention or BoJ communication would extend USD/JPY downside.
NZD is already the weakest major; off-hours RBNZ comments can trigger another NZD leg.
ADP was ignored at -0.018%, but weak claims or a soft ISM could accelerate USD losses after DXY -0.129%.
risks.watch: Unemployment Claims forecast 205K, ISM Services PMI forecast 54.2

risks.why_it_matters: Brent rose +1.731% on geopolitical risk; a reversal would pressure CAD, NOK, and ZAR positioning.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: The next Asia window starts with RBNZ Gov Breman at 22:10, keeping NZD the focal point after today's -0.966% underperformance. CHF CPI m/m at 08:30 (forecast 0.0%, previous -0.1%) can move USD/CHF and EUR/CHF. US Unemployment Claims at 205K and ISM Services PMI at 54.2 are the main USD inputs; strong data could floor the dollar after the ADP miss was ignored.
